chapter_name: Population Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition (India)
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the demographic landscape of India, understanding where people live, how fast the population is growing, and what makes up its diverse society!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: India's population is highly uneven. States like UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, and West Bengal have massive populations due to fertile plains and resources, while states like Arunachal Pradesh are sparsely populated.

India is highly dense. Geographers look at 'Physiological density' (population ÷ net sown area) and 'Agricultural density' (agricultural population ÷ net cultivable area) to understand real pressure on agricultural land.
India's population history has 4 phases: Stagnant (1901-21), Steady growth (1921-51), Rapid high growth/Population Explosion (1951-81), and High but decelerating growth (1981-present).
Analyzing the population based on age, sex, residence (Rural vs Urban), language (Linguistic families), and religion. India has incredible linguistic and religious diversity.

The population is divided into Main workers (work > 6 months), Marginal workers (work < 6 months), and Non-workers. A large chunk of India's workforce is still engaged in the primary sector (agriculture).

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ The Language Tree
fun_activity.instructions: India has 22 scheduled languages! Find out which 'Linguistic Family' your mother tongue belongs to (e.g., Indo-European, Dravidian, Austric, or Sino-Tibetan).

exam_tips: 📌 1921 is known as the 'demographic divide' in India because population growth was negative before it and consistently positive after.
📌 Be able to define and distinguish between Physiological Density and Agricultural Density.
📌 Memorize the four phases of India's population growth and the reasons behind the 'Population Explosion' phase.
quick_recap: ⭐ Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India.
⭐ A high proportion of marginal workers and non-workers indicates economic challenges and unemployment.
⭐ The Indo-European (Aryan) linguistic family is spoken by the largest percentage of Indians (around 73%).
